title: Not All Pixels are Equal: Learning Pixel Hardness for Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Gradient-isolated branch learns a stable pixel hardness map by maximising hardness-weighted loss while the seg head minimises it.
adaptation: Targets thin parts (gridline, crack). On jittered crack labels hard pixels are often label noise: restrict hardness weighting to non-crack classes or to pixels within 2 px of the label.
min_experiment: Arm: hardness branch on house model, 3 seeds; baseline SUP100; metric gridline IoU and mIoU_rob, crack IoU guard; kill if mIoU_rob < +0.01.
evidence: R: +1.37 mIoU on average over popular segmentation models on Cityscapes; generalises across domains.
